programmes.t: The FBI Files: A Stranger in Town
programmes.d: She appeared on the highway in the spring, a young woman, her life cut short, her past and her identity a mystery. Only by finding out who she was could we ever hope to find her killer.
A teenage immigrant found herself an innocent victim of drug trafficking.

Despite what you see in the movies, most bank robbers come in quietly, pass a note, and slip away. They want cash, not bloodshed. But in Richmond, Virginia, a pair of gunmen entered a bank with their guns blazing.
Experts examine a bomb left by robbers on a teller's counter.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Polly Klaas: Kidnapped
programmes.d: On October 1, 1993, a stranger abducted 12-year-old Polly Klaas during a slumber party in her home.
A cross-country crime spree over a Labor Day weekend terrorized the nation.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: John Gotti: Convicted
programmes.d: John Gotti was ambitious, powerful and ruthless. He ruled with flash and conspicuous style, playing celebrity with the media and cat and mouse with the FBI. They called John Gotti the Teflon Don. Serious charges just wouldn't stick.
A man gives police conflicting accounts of what happened to his niece.
In the early 1990's, a serial killer stalked lone victims in the dead of night, his hunting ground the suburbs of Washington, D.C., his target, anyone who owned a car.
In the summer of 1998, a wealthy woman disappeared from her home in Jackson, Mississippi.
In 1984, in South Florida, a rapist and murderer was on the loose. The killer was a ruthless and terrifying predator, the newest member of an infamous group known as serial killers.
In Arizona, a shipment of money vanished without a trace, along with the two men hired to guard it.
In 1984, a tragic murder led agents into the frightening world of domestic terrorism. Law enforcement vowed to dismantle the violent faction that claimed responsibility.
A pair of convicted felons escaped the custody of a local deputy and fled across the country.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: The Crazy Don
programmes.d: To the FBI, he was believed to be the boss of New York's most powerful mafia organization: the Genovese crime family. Was Gigante crazy or was his behavior a shrewd attempt to disguise his position as a ruthless mafia boss?
In 1992, a young mother was gunned down in front of her children and police were left baffled.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: A Family Torn
programmes.d: The parents of 11 yr. old Brittany Martinez knew their daughter was no runaway. Something had happened to her, something terrible. When they failed to find Brittany in their quiet Illinois neighborhood, they called the police.
A wealthy young woman was abducted in front of her in-laws' home.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: First and Kennedy Street Crew
programmes.d: In the early 1990's, Washington, D.C., became the murder capital of the nation. Few were left untouched by gang violence, which was ignited by the drug trade. By 1994, that violence would strike at the very heart of law enforcement.
Two young men go on a spree of robbery, kidnapping and murder, then they disappear.
Money may not be the root of all evil, but for some men, a million dollars is enough to justify murder. Even men sworn to uphold the law can sometimes be tempted.
In the 1980s, Florida's cocaine imports were among the highest in the nation.

A series of armored car heists and bloody shoot-outs shocked law enforcement. The brutal violence of the crimes suggested a motive more complex than greed. When the robbers started targeting police, the FBI took charge.
A young woman went missing from her home on a bright spring morning.
A woman and her infant son vanish. The husband is frantic. The clues are scarce, but hopes linger, even as the hours and days tick by without a word. Was she on the run, or the victim of foul play?
In July 1997, three people were shot to death at a Georgetown coffee shop.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Cracking The Cartel
programmes.d: A mother and child are kidnapped, a bystander is murdered. Violence such as this shattered a quiet Texas neighborhood and exposed a drug cartel that flourished where it was least expected.
In 1986, a psychotic killer shot and killed a police officer at point-blank range.

In Arizona, an armored van loaded with cash failed to reach its destination. Authorities suspected an inside job. When the vehicle was recovered with the drivers and the cash missing, those suspicions grew even more.
Mir Qazi brutally gunned down two members of the CIA as they waited in their cars at a stoplight.

Over a thousand hunting accidents are reported in the United States each year. Fewer than ten percent of them are fatal. But when one hunter's death seemed suspicious, the FBI was called in to investigate.
On the day before Thanksgiving, a mother discovered her young son was missing from school.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Above the Law
programmes.d: California Highway Patrolman George Gwaltney discovered the body of 23-year-old Robin Bishop near her car on a remote desert highway.
In the upscale town of Lodi, California, a 12-year-old girl was taken from her home.

In 1995, our nation's capital was also our nation's murder capital. Even the police weren't safe. While Washington, DC, law enforcement targeted criminals, the criminals targeted law enforcement, even gunning down officers on patrol.
In rural Texas, a millionaire's teenage daughter was kidnapped on her way to school.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Held For Ransom
programmes.d: Wealth has its rewards, but it also brings its dangers. Kidnapping is one of them. No ordeal is more horrifying for a family than to have a child taken.
In September 1997, a team of masked gunmen robbed an armored car facility in Los Angeles.

When a family was murdered in Arkansas, it seemed like an isolated event. But soon the crime was revealed to be part of an ever-widening circle of violence that defined a new age of domestic terrorism.
Authorities range from Alabama to Virginia in search of murder suspects.
When three people were found murdered in their home, it appeared like a burglary gone awry. But a crime this horrific deserved a closer look.
What begins as a routine arrest turns into a statewide manhunt.

Two armed bank robbers hit a Seattle bank taking over 150,000 dollars. Before they can escape police confront them and the pair splits up. As authorities search block by block they learn one was a career criminal with a long history of violence.
Violent criminal on the run.

programmes.t: The FBI Files: Melissa Brannen: Missing
programmes.d: In 1989, residents of a close-knit apartment community in Virginia gathered for a holiday celebration. For Tammy Brannen and five-year-old daughter Melissa, Christmas was always a special time. Then, without warning, the little girl was gone.
Wisconsin's largest bank robbery.

In the summer of 1999, a brutal serial killer who traveled by train terrorized Texas.
